data_quote: [primary juvenile period: abstract, pdf p. 2] The primary juvenile period of plants was 7-8 years, within the period of likely return fire intervals in the study area.; [primary juvenile period: text, pdf p. 7] As it takes over 6 months for fruits to mature and as the first flowering effectively produced almost no seed, we consider the first effective fruit set was some 7-8 years after the fire.; [first flowering: text, pdf p. 6] No plants flowered until 6 years after the fire.; [sample size: methods, pdf p. 4] New seedlings (71) were identified by their distinctive cotyledons.; [fire response: methods, pdf p. 3] It is a fire sensitive obligate seeder, common in the understorey in heath and woodlands along the east coast and ranges of New South Wales, Australia (Weston 2002).; [site: methods, pdf p. 3] We examined a population of *P. lanceolata* at one site within Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park 20 km north of Sydney (33°53' E, 151°13' S) southeastern Australia. ... The site was burnt by an extensive summer (January) wildfire in 1994 that burnt all the surrounding habitat.

data_quote: [fire response: text, p. 39] While the fire killed many of the existing *Senecio* plants some survived by resprouting from a rootstock.; [fire response: text, p. 42] This study indicates that *S. garlandii* is principally a seeder although some plants function as sprouters after a low-intensity fire.; [site: text, p. 36] At only 340 ha, The Rock Nature Reserve (lat. 35° 16' S, long. 147° 05' E) is a small island of remnant native vegetation, surrounded by extensive agricultural lands. ... After less than 75 mm of rain during November 1990 to March 1991 (average 208 mm for this period) the first major fire (15–17 March 1991) in 40 years burnt more than 90% of The Rock Nature Reserve (personal observation).; [rainfall post fire: text, p. 43] This suggests that a low fire intensity, combined with more than the about 25 mm of rainfall received in the 2.5 months after the March fire (Fig. 2), then more *Senecio* rootstocks may have resprouted.
notes: fire_response_categorical_surv1: most plants killed, some resprouted from rootstocks (less than 5% of the original population remained in leaf after the fire, p. 35), mapped to O/r; flowering times not filled because no time value is printed: no seedlings flowered in their first summer, 44% of the 143 surviving seedlings flowered in mid-december 1992 (their second year) and over 95% of 122 surviving plants had flowered in december 1993 (third summer) (p. 40); resprouting rootstocks had flower primordia about 6 weeks after early september 1991 and had finished flowering by late november 1991 (p. 39; p. 40); rainfall_post_fire_mm printed 'about 25 mm'; fire_season_categorical derived from fire date 15-17 march 1991; fire severity not stated for this fire: the paper suggests a low fire intensity would have allowed more rootstocks to resprout (p. 43); fire type not stated ('first major fire in 40 years'); rainfall from forest hill, wagga wagga, 35 km ne of the site
source: burrows, g. e. (1995). post-fire regeneration and growth of senecio garlandii (asteraceae) - a vulnerable plant of the south western slopes, nsw. cunninghamia, 4(1), 35-44.
